pathway.title: CSS
pathway.description: A complete standalone CSS course with practical lessons, examples, guided activities and assessment.

course.title: CSS — Intermediate
course.dependencies: A modern browser; no framework required.
course.short_description: A complete standalone CSS course with practical lessons, examples, guided activities and assessment.
course.prerequisites: Comfort with CSS fundamentals and the previous level.
learning_outcomes: Build correct, meaningful and accessible interfaces.
Apply the course concepts in practical projects.
Test, review and explain design decisions.

topics.title: Selectors and the cascade
topics.description: CSS matches elements with selectors and applies declarations. When rules conflict, the cascade considers specificity and source order. Keep selectors understandable so styles remain maintainable.

lesson.title: Selectors and the cascade
objectives: Explain selectors and the cascade using clear terminology.
Apply selectors and the cascade in a small practical task.
Test and explain the result of the implementation.

blocks.title: Concepts and practical context
blocks.body: CSS matches elements with selectors and applies declarations. When rules conflict, the cascade considers specificity and source order. Keep selectors understandable so styles remain maintainable.

blocks.title: A small practical example
blocks.expected_output: The card and its heading receive the declared styles.
blocks.explanation: Read the example line by line. Identify the structure, the rule being demonstrated, and the part you could change safely.

blocks.title: Guided practical activity
instructions: Style a course card using a class selector, then style its heading without using unnecessarily specific selectors.
success_checks: The implementation matches the stated goal.
The learner checks both a normal case and one boundary case.
The learner can explain the important lines or declarations.

items.prompt: Which choice best demonstrates the idea in Selectors and the cascade?

choices.text: Use clear selectors and understand which rule wins.
Add unrelated code until the page appears different.
Skip testing because the example worked once.

items.explanation: The correct choice applies the concept deliberately and checks its result.

topics.title: Box model and spacing
topics.description: Every element participates in the box model: content, padding, border and margin. Use box-sizing deliberately and build spacing from a consistent scale.

lesson.title: Box model and spacing
objectives: Explain box model and spacing using clear terminology.
Apply box model and spacing in a small practical task.
Test and explain the result of the implementation.

blocks.title: Concepts and practical context
blocks.body: Every element participates in the box model: content, padding, border and margin. Use box-sizing deliberately and build spacing from a consistent scale.

blocks.title: A small practical example
blocks.code:
* { box-sizing: border-box; }
.card { padding: 1.5rem; margin: 1rem 0; border: 1px solid #ddd; }
blocks.expected_output: A predictable card box with internal and external spacing.
blocks.explanation: Read the example line by line. Identify the structure, the rule being demonstrated, and the part you could change safely.

blocks.title: Guided practical activity
instructions: Create a lesson card with readable padding, a subtle border and consistent vertical spacing.
success_checks: The implementation matches the stated goal.
The learner checks both a normal case and one boundary case.
The learner can explain the important lines or declarations.

items.prompt: Which choice best demonstrates the idea in Box model and spacing?

choices.text: Explain the difference between padding, border and margin.
Add unrelated code until the page appears different.
Skip testing because the example worked once.

items.explanation: The correct choice applies the concept deliberately and checks its result.

topics.title: Flexbox and Grid
topics.description: Flexbox is useful for one-dimensional alignment; Grid is useful for two-dimensional page and card layouts. Both adapt to available space and reduce fragile positioning.

lesson.title: Flexbox and Grid
objectives: Explain flexbox and grid using clear terminology.
Apply flexbox and grid in a small practical task.
Test and explain the result of the implementation.

blocks.title: Concepts and practical context
blocks.body: Flexbox is useful for one-dimensional alignment; Grid is useful for two-dimensional page and card layouts. Both adapt to available space and reduce fragile positioning.

blocks.title: A small practical example
blocks.code:
.cards { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 1rem; }
.nav { display: flex; gap: 1rem; align-items: center; }
blocks.expected_output: A three-column grid and aligned navigation.
blocks.explanation: Read the example line by line. Identify the structure, the rule being demonstrated, and the part you could change safely.

blocks.title: Guided practical activity
instructions: Build a course-card grid that becomes one column on narrow screens and a navigation row that aligns vertically.
success_checks: The implementation matches the stated goal.
The learner checks both a normal case and one boundary case.
The learner can explain the important lines or declarations.

items.prompt: Which choice best demonstrates the idea in Flexbox and Grid?

choices.text: Choose Grid for the card layout and Flexbox for the navigation alignment.
Add unrelated code until the page appears different.
Skip testing because the example worked once.

items.explanation: The correct choice applies the concept deliberately and checks its result.

topics.title: Responsive design and accessibility
topics.description: Responsive design adapts content to different viewports. Start mobile-first, then add enhancements at larger widths. Focus states, contrast and reduced motion are part of professional CSS.

lesson.title: Responsive design and accessibility
objectives: Explain responsive design and accessibility using clear terminology.
Apply responsive design and accessibility in a small practical task.
Test and explain the result of the implementation.

blocks.title: Concepts and practical context
blocks.body: Responsive design adapts content to different viewports. Start mobile-first, then add enhancements at larger widths. Focus states, contrast and reduced motion are part of professional CSS.

blocks.title: A small practical example
blocks.expected_output: The page gains space on larger screens while respecting reduced motion.
blocks.explanation: Read the example line by line. Identify the structure, the rule being demonstrated, and the part you could change safely.

blocks.title: Guided practical activity
instructions: Make a lesson page mobile-first, add a desktop breakpoint, visible keyboard focus and a reduced-motion rule.
success_checks: The implementation matches the stated goal.
The learner checks both a normal case and one boundary case.
The learner can explain the important lines or declarations.

items.prompt: Which choice best demonstrates the idea in Responsive design and accessibility?

choices.text: Test multiple widths and preserve usable focus and readable contrast.
Add unrelated code until the page appears different.
Skip testing because the example worked once.

items.explanation: The correct choice applies the concept deliberately and checks its result.

practical_project.title: CSS Intermediate Capstone
practical_project.brief: Build CSS Intermediate Capstone using the skills from this course. Include a short explanation of your decisions, test the result on mobile and desktop, and make a small accessibility review.

final_assessment.title: CSS — Intermediate final assessment
final_assessment.instructions: Complete the practical task, then answer the knowledge checks and explain two implementation decisions.
final_assessment.passing_guidance: Demonstrate the required structure, test the result, and explain why the chosen approach is appropriate.

teacher_materials.notes: Encourage learners to build from semantic structure, test incrementally, and explain their choices rather than copying patterns without understanding them.
teacher_materials.safety: Use only learner-owned or authorised files and environments.

provenance.content_note: Standalone HTML/CSS curriculum added to complement the existing Web Development pathway.
